lines: Class one. Sit. Or stand, you have no chairs.
Today: rocks. Every rock here started as melted stone.
Melted stone that cools slowly grows big crystals.
Cooled fast, at the surface: tiny crystals, or none.
Glass, even. Look through the hand lens and you will see.
There are rocks lying about outside.
Pick them up. Test them. Use the key in your notebook.

task.text: Identify two different rocks in the lab.

lines: Field trip. Mind the ground, it is thin here.
Hot rock below. Water above. That is a geyser.
The water heats in a narrow throat, deep down.
It flashes to steam and up it all goes.
Then the throat is empty, and it fills again.
lesson.note: A geyser: narrow throat, heat, steam, then empty, then refill.

lines: Three pools. One spouts. One is only warm water.
One has a stone jammed in its throat.
When would you dare reach in? Think. Then do it.

leave: I will be at the ship. Do not get scalded.

entry.name: Why the geyser spouts
entry.line: Pulled the stone right after the big one blew: the throat was empty. It spouts again.

blocked.name: Blocked pool
look: A round pool with a white crust round its rim.
A stone sits jammed in the throat.
The water trembles, but never spouts.

reply: Each time the big geyser spouts,
this pool drops a hand's width.
Then it creeps back up. Same plumbing.

still.name: Warm pool
look: Flat, steaming, no crust on the rim.

reply: No stone, no throat. This one is only a pool.
The big geyser spouts. This pool does nothing.

pullSolved: The throat is empty. The stone comes out easily.
A rumble. The water drops, then it SPOUTS.
Two geysers. The whole field is steaming.
pullEarly: You reach in. The water surges up, scalding.
pullDone: It spouts on its own now. Leave it be.

lines: Class two. You have been outside. Good.
A survey is not a walk. It is a walk with a map.
Your map has letters across and numbers down.
A letter and a number name one square: C3, say.
Write where things are, not just what they are.
Three things outside, noticed and written down.
That is your task. Water counts. Stones count.

task.text: Look closely at three things and write them in the notebook.

lines: Field trip. Speak up, the water is loud.
Water is lazy. It only ever goes downhill.
A map draws height as lines. Cross one, you climb.
Lines close together: steep. Far apart: flat.
Where the ground dips, water will follow it.
lesson.note: Contour lines show height. Water never climbs.

lines: In spring the melt comes down this river.
Gunnar's pens sit in a hollow off to one side.
Three banks of earth. Put them where it counts.

task.text: Plan the banks so the melt misses the pens.

leave: The planning table is by the bank. I will be at the ship.

entry.name: Where the melt goes
entry.line: Banked the side channel at its lip. Water never climbs, so the pens stay dry.

table.name: Planning table
look: A map of the valley, weighted down with stones.
Lines mark the height of the land.

lines.intro: Place up to three banks. Then run the melt and watch where it goes.
lines.success: The melt goes round. The pens stay dry. Gunnar owes you a coffee.
lines.pensFlooded: The pens are under water. The sheep are on the roof. Move the banks and try again.
lines.blocked: You dammed the river itself. The melt has to reach the sea somewhere. Try again.
lines.noBanks: No banks left. Pick one up (Enter on it) to move it.

lines: Class three. People.
They are the hardest part of any planet.
Nobody here owes you anything. Say hello anyway.
Come back tomorrow and say it again.
When they know you, they will tell you what maps cannot.
Learn one true thing from a person in this town.
Not from a sign. From a person.

task.text: Learn one thing from a person in town.

lines: Class four. Your map still has blank squares.
Blank squares are where surveys go to die.
The compass on your map points north.
North is the top of the map. Always, on this planet.
Walk the edges. Fill the blanks.
A third of the map, at least, before your final report.
And the final report is due at the end of day 90.

task.text: Explore at least a third of the map.

lines.classToday: Day {day}. You have class today. Come to the ship. On time.
lines.classMissed: You missed class yesterday. Here are my notes. Read them.
lines.taskGrace: Day {day}. Your task was due. Are you all right? One more chance: day {due}.
lines.taskMissed: Day {day}. Task not done: {task} It goes on your record.
lines.deadlineSoon: Reminder: final report at the end of day {due}. {left} day(s) left.
finalPass: That is a pass. You may stay as long as you like.
The next class begins when the term does.
finalFail: That is below the pass mark. You will retake the class.
Everything you have found stays. No more classes. Go and look.
retakePass: Passed. Took you a while. It took me longer, once.
lines.puzzleLocked: You do not know what you are looking at. Yet. Class first.
